ei.title: Chapter 3-08 2번: The Opportunity Cost of Limited Resources
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.

questions.passage: We have (A)[vast / scarce] forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the (B)[wilderness / civilization], and all of the (C)[accessible / restricted] recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 나라에 광대한(vast) 숲이 있지만, 황무지(wilderness)와 접근 가능한(accessible) 휴양을 모두 제공하기에는 충분하지 않다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① vast — civilization — accessible (B 반대: 황무지→문명)
❌ ② scarce — wilderness — accessible (A 반대: 광대한→부족한)
❌ ③ vast — wilderness — restricted (C 반대: 접근 가능한→제한된)
✅ ④ vast — wilderness — accessible — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water (A)[consumed / preserved] cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest (B)[renew / deplete] itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to (C)[allocate / waste] our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 소비된(consumed) 물은 식수로 사용될 수 없고, 숲이 스스로 갱신(renew)하도록 돕고, 제한된 자원을 어떻게 할당(allocate)할지 선택해야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① consumed — renew — waste (C 반대: 할당하다→낭비하다)
❌ ② preserved — renew — allocate (A 반대: 소비된→보존된)
❌ ③ consumed — deplete — allocate (B 반대: 갱신하다→고갈시키다)
✅ ④ consumed — renew — allocate — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or (A)[improve / neglect] trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air (B)[pollution / purification] downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our (C)[limited / abundant] resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 등산로와 야영지를 개선(improve)하고, 대기 오염(pollution)이 발생하며, 제한된(limited) 자원을 어떻게 할당할지 선택해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① improve — pollution — limited — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② neglect — pollution — limited (A 반대: 개선하다→방치하다)
❌ ③ improve — purification — limited (B 반대: 오염→정화)
❌ ④ improve — pollution — abundant (C 반대: 제한된→풍부한)

questions.passage: We have ①<u>vast</u> forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the ②<u>wilderness</u>, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water ③<u>generated</u> cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to ④<u>allocate</u> our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '생성된(generated)'이 아니라 '소비된(consumed)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 쌀 재배에 사용된 물은 소비되어 식수로 사용될 수 없다.
det.analysis:
① vast — 광대한, 원문 일치
② wilderness — 황무지, 원문 일치
③ generated — 원문은 consumed(소비된) ←정답
④ allocate — 할당하다, 원문 일치

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we ①<u>log</u> trees, build roads, or ②<u>damage</u> trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of ③<u>fresh</u> water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest ④<u>renew</u> itself, we will have air pollution downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make choices about how to allocate our limited resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '손상시키다(damage)'가 아니라 '개선하다(improve)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 등산로와 야영지를 개선한다는 맥락이다.
det.analysis:
① log — 벌목하다, 원문 일치
② damage — 원문은 improve(개선하다) ←정답
③ fresh — 신선한, 원문 일치
④ renew — 갱신하다, 원문 일치

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the ①<u>accessible</u> recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. Similarly, we have large amounts of fresh water, but if we use water to grow rice in California, the water consumed cannot be used for drinking water in California cities. If we use fire to help a forest renew itself, we will have air ②<u>pollution</u> downwind while the fire burns. We have many goals, so we have to make ③<u>choices</u> about how to allocate our ④<u>unlimited</u> resources. The cost of those choices is what we give up — the cost of opportunities lost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '무한한(unlimited)'이 아니라 '제한된(limited)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 자원이 제한되어 있기 때문에 선택을 해야 한다.
det.analysis:
① accessible — 접근 가능한, 원문 일치
② pollution — 오염, 원문 일치
③ choices — 선택, 원문 일치
④ unlimited — 원문은 limited(제한된) ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:

❌ ② resources — 자원 (뒷문장 개념, 여기서는 자연 상태 상실)
✅ ③ wilderness — 황무지 ←정답
❌ ④ pollution — 오염 (잃는 대상이 아님)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 많은 목표가 있기 때문에 제한된 자원을 어떻게 할당(allocate)할지 선택해야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① consume — 소비하다 (자원 관리의 핵심은 배분이지 소비가 아님)
✅ ② allocate — 할당하다 ←정답
❌ ③ improve — 개선하다 (자원을 개선하는 것이 아닌 배분하는 것)
❌ ④ renew — 갱신하다 (갱신이 아닌 배분 선택의 문맥)
det.tip: how to allocate our limited resources = 제한된 자원을 어떻게 할당할지

❌ ② trails — 등산로 (구체적 시설이지 포괄적 목적이 아님)
❌ ③ opportunities — 기회 (뒷문장 개념, 여기서는 숲의 용도)
✅ ④ recreation — 휴양 ←정답

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 vast의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: vast = 광대한 → immense(거대한, 막대한)
det.analysis:
❌ ① narrow — 좁은 (반의어 방향)
✅ ② immense — 거대한 ←정답
❌ ③ dense — 밀집한 (크기가 아닌 밀도)
❌ ④ remote — 먼, 외진 (크기가 아닌 거리)

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. As soon as we log trees, build roads, or improve trails and campsites, we lose some wilderness. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 consumed의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: consumed = 소비된 → used up(다 써버린)
det.analysis:
❌ ① stored — 저장된 (소비와 반대 방향)
❌ ② collected — 수집된 (의미축 다름)
✅ ③ used up — 다 써버린 ←정답
❌ ④ filtered — 여과된 (의미축 다름)

questions.passage: We have vast forests in this country but not enough to provide all of the wood, all of the wilderness, and all of the accessible recreation that we want. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 allocate의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: allocate = 할당하다 → distribute(분배하다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① distribute — 분배하다 ←정답
❌ ② accumulate — 축적하다 (배분이 아닌 모으는 것)
❌ ③ deplete — 고갈시키다 (의미축 다름)
❌ ④ evaluate — 평가하다 (의미축 다름)

det.korean: limited(제한된) ↔ boundless(무한한)
det.analysis:
✅ ① boundless — 무한한 ←정답
❌ ② reduced — 축소된 (동의어 방향)
❌ ③ valuable — 가치 있는 (의미축 다름)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 accessible의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: accessible(접근 가능한) ↔ exclusive(배타적인, 독점적인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① available — 이용 가능한 (동의어 방향)
✅ ② exclusive — 배타적인, 독점적인 ←정답
❌ ③ popular — 인기 있는 (의미축 다름)
❌ ④ inaccessible — 접근 불가능한 (접두사 조작형 금지 S-ANTONYM-PREFIX)

questions.passage:
(A) As soon as we <u>log</u> trees, build roads, or improve trails, we lose some wilderness.

(B) The captain asked the crew to <u>log</u> the ship's position every hour during the voyage.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 log의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 나무를 벌목하다(cut down trees) / (B) 선박 위치를 기록하다(record)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 벌목하다 — 기록하다 ←정답
❌ ② 기록하다 — 벌목하다 (의미 뒤바뀜)
❌ ③ 벌목하다 — 운반하다 (B는 기록하는 행위)
❌ ④ 운반하다 — 기록하다 (A는 벌목하는 행위)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to make something new again or to restore it to a good condition"

det.korean: 무언가를 다시 새롭게 만들거나 좋은 상태로 회복시키다 → renew(갱신하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① consume — 소비하다 (회복이 아닌 사용)
❌ ② allocate — 할당하다 (회복이 아닌 배분)
❌ ③ pollution — 오염 (명사이며 회복과 반대)
✅ ④ renew — 갱신하다 ←정답
det.tip: renew = 새롭게 하다, 갱신하다 (restore to a good condition)

det.korean: 접근 가능한(accessible) 휴양 → access(명사/동사) → accessible(형용사)
